title: 1966 AHSME Problem 37
statement: Three men, Alpha, Beta, and Gamma, working together, do a job in \(6\) hours less time than Alpha alone, in \(1\) hour less time than Beta alone, and in one-half the time needed by Gamma when working alone. Let \(h\) be the number of hours needed by Alpha and Beta, working together, to do the job. Then \(h\) equals:

solutions.text:
If all three together take \(t\) hours, then \[ \frac1{t+6}+\frac1{t+1}+\frac1{2t}=\frac1t. \] This simplifies to \(3t^2+7t-6=0,\) so \(t=\frac{2}{3}.\) Alpha and Beta alone take \(\frac{20}{3}\) and \(\frac{5}{3}\) hours, so their combined rate is \(\frac{3}{20}+\frac{3}{5}=\frac{3}{4}.\) Hence \(h=\frac{4}{3}.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is C.
hints: Let \(t\) be the time all three take together
Their individual times are \(t+6,\) \(t+1,\) and \(2t\); add reciprocal rates
